parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the need to reimplement yaml.safe_load plus yaml.dump in pure ESM JavaScript, place all files in /output, parse --a manually, avoid external dependencies, and create test8.mjs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent wrote shared types itself, then split work across four children: resolver.mjs, parser.mjs, emitter.mjs, and argparse.mjs, with the parent implicitly retaining final integration and entry assembly.
parallel.implementation: Two children completed useful modules, argparse.mjs and resolver.mjs. The parser and emitter children spent their windows probing PyYAML behavior and did not finish their modules before cancellation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No final integration occurred. Artifact validation found only types.mjs, argparse.mjs, and resolver.mjs, with the required test8.mjs entry absent.
parallel.verification: Completed children ran local probe harnesses for their modules, but there was no integrated node test8.mjs verification because the required parser, emitter, and entry point were missing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Parser, emitter, and test8.mjs were absent; two implementation children were stopped; official evaluation completed but passed no testcases.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same PyYAML safe_load plus dump behavior, ESM-only output, no external dependencies, manual --a parsing, and /output placement requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run kept all ownership in one actor, using repeated black-box probes to map PyYAML semantics before attempting to write the full implementation itself.
serial.implementation: The serial actor accumulated a large behavioral map for scalars, collections, anchors, tags, timestamps, and argparse edge cases but did not write implementation files before cancellation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: There was no integration phase and no delivered files. Artifact validation found an empty output artifact with no test8.mjs.
serial.verification: Serial verification consisted of executable probes during analysis; there was no runnable JavaScript solution and no integrated verification of delivered code.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: All implementation and delivery work remained unfinished at closure, so the official evaluator had no usable artifact and passed no tests.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept the entire problem in the main actor and used no children or delegation.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial held the behavioral findings in one context, with no inter-agent interface or handoff boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had cross-agent coordination boundaries and a temporary-file contamination episode; serial had no such boundary but also no completed implementation.

comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached a partial modular implementation; serial remained at analysis/probing with no delivered files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received completed argparse and resolver reports, then the parser and emitter child results failed after active cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results or handoffs, only a single main trajectory that was canceled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's required implementation lifecycle depended on child returns and stalled on incomplete children; serial had no result lifecycle beyond its own unfinished run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote shared /output modules and also collided through a shared /tmp/probe.sh scratch tool that one child consumed as its own.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor and had no cross-agent shared-state collision, but also never produced an artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-environment contamination event; serial avoided that class of issue by not delegating.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran many reference probes but had no delivered JavaScript implementation to verify.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had localized module checks without whole-solution acceptance; serial had only exploratory probes and no artifact verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after four subagents, many tool calls, and nearly four million tokens; two active children were stopped.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but with one actor, no delegation, and a smaller request/token footprint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget was spread across child modules and ended with partial files plus failed child returns; serial budget was spent in one long analysis path with no files.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail, not discordant: both completed evaluation and passed 0 of 165 samples. The parallel run produced a partial modular artifact but missed the required entry point and two central modules; the serial run produced no artifact files at all. These are materially different failure paths, but neither yielded a runnable solution.
parallel_contributors: Overbroad parser and emitter children did not checkpoint usable modules before cancellation.
A shared /tmp/probe.sh leaked across children and contaminated emitter probing.
serial_contributors: The monolithic serial actor spent the run probing behavior and did not write deliverable files.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered resolver and argparse modules but no parser, emitter, or test8.mjs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns describe parallel adverse process consequences only

candidates.reason: Implementation owners existed: the parent wrote types and delegated resolver, parser, emitter, and argparse modules.
The parent retained the final integration role; the issue was that required child modules never arrived, not that integration was unassigned.
The parent described a final integration and entry-file phase; final assembly was not ownerless, it was blocked by unfinished children.
End-to-end ownership remained with the parent, which planned delegation and final integration; the pipeline did not lack an owner.
The parent did explore and write types before delegation, but productive child implementation later ran in parallel rather than being wholly blocked behind one mandatory preflight.
The parallel children performed overlapping implementation and probing; the run was not only an investigation phase followed by deferred implementation.
The critical parser and emitter paths were assigned active owners; the better fit is the oversized scope of those child tasks, not lack of capacity on an unserved path.
Four children alone does not prove excessive breadth; the concrete failure was that two individual child scopes were too broad to finish or checkpoint.
The parser and emitter children each received a whole PyYAML subsystem scope, spent the available window probing, and never produced usable modules before cancellation.
candidates.realized_consequence: Required parser, emitter, and entry modules were missing from the final artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: The explicit stop is the same chain's terminal event; the directly actionable boundary is the overbroad child scope with no usable checkpoint.

candidates.reason: The child briefs included task, environment, module, and verification requirements; failures came from scope size and lifecycle, not a known requirement omitted from the brief.
The parent established shared types and module names; no incompatible completed components required unplanned reconciliation.
No known requirement or finding is shown disappearing through transfer; the missing modules were never completed.
Completed child reports were not too large for the parent to reduce; the blocking work was unfinished parser and emitter implementation.
No actor consumed a returned handoff describing a superseded workspace state.
No incompatible completed handoffs reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
The parallel parent did not present the whole task as complete; the run was canceled with an incomplete artifact.
There was no replacement child or retry cycle that repeated prior work without inherited findings.

candidates.reason: Parser and emitter were explicitly stopped, but that is the same timeout chain as the retained oversized child tasks and is not counted separately.
No complete or mutually compatible component set existed for final placement because parser and emitter were unfinished.
No result was merged after an integrated verification pass; integrated verification never occurred.
Completed resolver and argparse modules were present in the artifact; missing parser and emitter were not completed implementations awaiting join.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent.
The child failures arrived at global cancellation with no separate post-failure decision window; this is the same chain as the oversized child allocation.
Completed resolver and argparse child outputs remained in the artifact and were not ignored in favor of inconsistent work.
The timeout symptoms belong to the retained oversized-child chain; there is no separate available progress inspection episode that would change closure.
Children owned distinct output modules; no competing implementation files claimed the same delivered behavior.
The shared /tmp/probe.sh problem involved consuming a leaked temporary tool; Artifact Leakage is more specific than a same-source edit collision.
No non-entry library or module source produced by one child was proven replaced by another.
No required executable or submitted entry artifact was overwritten; the required entry was absent.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced current final outputs.
The concrete shared-state harm is the temporary probe artifact leaking into another child, so the contamination label is more specific.
A scratch probe script generated by one parallel child was later consumed by the emitter child as if it were its own probe harness, contaminating its probing results.

candidates.near_match_reason: The same path is part of the evidence, but the realized harm is cross-agent consumption of a leaked temporary tool.
